data.title: Tinea capitis — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 12 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Tinea capitis** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. Who gets tinea capitis and why mostly children?**
- Prepubertal children (3–7 years); rare after puberty because sebum fatty acids (fungistatic) increase
- Adults: post-menopausal women, immunosuppressed

**Q2. Classify tinea capitis by hair invasion (PYQ).**
- Ectothrix: arthroconidia outside the shaft, cuticle destroyed — Microsporum (M. canis, M. audouinii; fluoresce green) and T. mentagrophytes, T. verrucosum (non-fluorescent large-spored)
- Endothrix: arthroconidia inside the shaft, cuticle intact — T. tonsurans, T. violaceum (commonest in India), T. soudanense; 'black dot' type; non-fluorescent
- Favic: T. schoenleinii — hyphae and air spaces inside hair; dull green fluorescence

**Q3. Describe the clinical types.**
- Non-inflammatory: grey patch (Microsporum — scaly round patches with broken dull hairs), black dot (endothrix — hairs break at scalp surface), seborrhoeic/diffuse scaling type (mimics dandruff), alopecia areata-like
- Inflammatory: kerion (boggy, tender, pustular mass with loose hairs, lymphadenopathy — zoophilic species; may scar), agminate folliculitis
- Favus: yellow cup-shaped crusts (scutula) around hairs, mousy odour, scarring alopecia

**Q4. What is a kerion? Should it be incised?**
- Intense delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction to zoophilic/geophilic dermatophytes producing a painful boggy swelling with pus-discharging follicles
- Do not incise (it is not bacterial abscess); treat with systemic antifungal ± short oral steroid for severe inflammation; can cause scarring alopecia

**Q5. Investigations.**
- Wood's lamp: green (Microsporum), dull green (favus), none (Trichophyton)
- KOH mount of plucked hairs and scales — ecto/endothrix spores
- Culture of hairs/scales (brush or cotton swab method) to identify species — important for choice of drug and to trace animal source
- Trichoscopy: comma hairs, corkscrew hairs, zig-zag hairs, Morse-code hairs, broken/black dots, bar-code hairs

**Q6. Differential diagnosis.**
- Seborrhoeic dermatitis, psoriasis (silvery scales, hairs intact), alopecia areata (no scaling, exclamation-mark hairs), trichotillomania (bizarre shapes, hairs of varying length), pityriasis amiantacea, atopic dermatitis, impetigo/folliculitis (kerion), discoid lupus, lichen planopilaris, secondary syphilis (moth-eaten alopecia)

**Q7. Treatment — choose the drug by organism.**
- Oral therapy is always needed (topicals do not penetrate the follicle)
- Griseofulvin (ultra-micro/micro) 20–25 mg/kg/day for 6–8 weeks (or longer) with fatty meal — best for Microsporum
- Terbinafine by weight for 2–4 weeks (Trichophyton) — <20 kg 62.5 mg, 20–40 kg 125 mg, >40 kg 250 mg/day; Microsporum needs longer
- Itraconazole 5 mg/kg/day 4–6 weeks or pulses; fluconazole 6 mg/kg/day 3–6 weeks
- Adjunct: ketoconazole 2%/selenium sulphide 2.5% shampoo twice weekly for patient and family to reduce spore shedding
- Examine and treat household contacts and pets; children can attend school once on treatment

**Q8. Side effects of griseofulvin.**
- Headache, GI upset, photosensitivity, urticaria, lupus flare, porphyria precipitation, enzyme inducer (reduces OCP and warfarin effect), disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol; avoid in pregnancy and men should avoid fathering a child for 6 months

**Q9. Endpoint of treatment?**
- Mycological cure (negative KOH and culture), not just clinical improvement

**Q10. What is tinea capitis in adults like?**
- Often atypical, diffuse scaling or mimics seborrhoeic dermatitis, folliculitis decalvans or DLE; usually Trichophyton (T. violaceum, T. tonsurans)

**Q11. What is the id reaction in tinea capitis?**
- Itchy papulovesicular eruption on face/trunk after starting treatment of kerion — immune hypersensitivity, not drug allergy; continue antifungal, topical steroid

**Q12. Prognosis of kerion?**
- Heals with variable permanent scarring alopecia if treatment is delayed

## Quick spotter facts
- Black dots in a patch of alopecia — endothrix (T. violaceum/tonsurans)
- Boggy pustular scalp mass — kerion (don't incise)
- Scutula + mousy odour — favus

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Superficial fungal infections). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
